Sample spaces and bar charts

Source: R/probability.R
probability.Rd

SampleSpace() is a rectangle that can be divided horizontally or vertically into parts with areas proportional to probabilities, with braces and labels. BarChart() is an Axes() with one bar per value.

Usage

SampleSpace(
  height = 3,
  width = 3,
  fill_color = DARK_GREY,
  fill_opacity = 1,
  stroke_width = 0.5,
  stroke_color = LIGHT_GREY,
  default_label_scale_val = 1,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'SampleSpace'
x[i, ...]

BarChart(
  values,
  bar_names = NULL,
  y_range = NULL,
  x_length = NULL,
  y_length = NULL,
  bar_colors = c("#003f5c", "#58508d", "#bc5090", "#ff6361", "#ffa600"),
  bar_width = 0.6,
  bar_fill_opacity = 0.7,
  bar_stroke_width = 3,
  x_axis_config = NULL,
  y_axis_config = NULL,
  tips = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

height, width

Size of the sample space.

fill_color, fill_opacity, stroke_width, stroke_color

Style.

default_label_scale_val

Scale applied to string labels.

...

Passed to Rectangle() or Axes().

x

A SampleSpace.

i

Index (1 based).

values

Numeric bar heights.

bar_names

Labels under the bars.

y_range

c(min, max, step) of the y axis; computed from values when NULL.

x_length, y_length

Axis lengths.

bar_colors

Colors spread over the bars as a gradient.

bar_width

Width of each bar in x units.

bar_fill_opacity, bar_stroke_width

Bar style.

x_axis_config, y_axis_config

Lists of NumberLine() arguments.

tips

Whether the axes get tips.

Value

A mobject.

Details

SampleSpace methods: add_title(), add_label(), complete_p_list(), get_horizontal_division(), get_vertical_division(), divide_horizontally(), divide_vertically(), get_side_braces_and_labels(), get_top_braces_and_labels(), get_bottom_braces_and_labels(), add_braces_and_labels(). Indexing space[i] returns the i-th part once the space is divided.

BarChart methods: get_bar_labels(), change_bar_values(). Bars are in the field bars.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Needs LaTeX and dvisvgm.
s <- SampleSpace()$divide_vertically(c(0.3, 0.7))
chart <- BarChart(c(1, 3, 2), bar_names = c("a", "b", "c"))
} # }
